Below is a step‑by‑step guide to send a welcome email to every new user that signs up on Replit. The example uses Firebase (Authentication + Firestore) + SendGrid for email. Feel free to swap out any service for one you already use (e.g. AWS SES, Mailgun, etc.). --- ## 1. Prerequisites | ✅ | Requirement | |----|-------------| | ✔️ | Replit account | | ✔️ | Firebase project (Auth + Firestore enabled) | | ✔️ | SendGrid API key (or another SMTP/API email provider) | | ✔️ | Node.js Replit environment (you can use the `replit.nix` or `Dockerfile`) | | ✔️ | Basic knowledge of JavaScript/Node.js | --- ## 2. Create the Replit Project 1. **Start a new Replit** - Choose **Node.js** template. 2. **Folder structure** ``` /api # Cloud functions / serverless functions └─ welcomeEmail.js /.env # Environment variable file (never commit) SENDGRID_API_KEY=xxxx FCM_API_KEY=xxxx FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=xxxx # Base64‑encoded JSON ``` --- ## 3. Configure Firebase 1. **Create a service account** - In Firebase console → Project Settings → Service accounts. - Generate new private key → download `serviceAccountKey.json`. 2. **Encode it** ```bash cat serviceAccountKey.json | base64 | pbcopy ``` Paste the Base64 string to `.env` as `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`. 3. **Add Auth trigger** - Replit uses **Cloud Functions for Firebase**. - Install Firebase CLI inside the Replit container: ```bash npm install -g firebase-tools ``` - Login and initialize: ```bash firebase login firebase init functions # choose JavaScript, do not use TypeScript, skip tests, confirm adding `node_modules` to .gitignore ``` This creates a `functions/` folder. We'll replace that with `api/`. 4. **Update `package.json` scripts** ```json "scripts": { "deploy": "firebase deploy --only functions", "start": "node api/welcomeEmail.js" } ``` --- ## 4. Install Dependencies ```bash npm install --save firebase-admin firebase-functions dotenv @sendgrid/mail ``` --- ## 5. Write the Welcome‑Email Function Create `api/welcomeEmail.js`: ```js // api/welcomeEmail.js require('dotenv').config(); const admin = require('firebase-admin'); const functions = require('firebase-functions'); const sgMail = require('@sendgrid/mail'); // Initialise Firebase Admin SDK const serviceAccount = JSON.parse( Buffer.from(process.env.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, 'base64').toString() ); admin.initializeApp({ credential: admin.credential.cert(serviceAccount), databaseURL: 'https://.firebaseio.com' }); // Initialise SendGrid sgMail.setApiKey(process.env.SENDGRID_API_KEY); // Cloud Function: Triggered on user creation exports.sendWelcomeEmail = functions.auth.user().onCreate((user) => { const email = user.email; const name = user.displayName || 'there'; const msg = { to: email, from: 'no-reply@yourapp.com', subject: '🎉 Welcome to YourApp!', text: `Hello ${name},\n\nThanks for joining our community! We're excited to have you on board.\n\nBest,\nThe YourApp Team`, html: `

Hello ${name},

Thanks for joining our community! We're excited to have you on board.

Best,
The YourApp Team

` }; return sgMail .send(msg) .then(() => console.log(`Welcome email sent to ${email}`)) .catch(err => { console.error('Error sending welcome email:', err); throw err; }); }); ``` **Notes** - Replace `` with your actual Firebase project ID. - Make sure the sending address (`no-reply@yourapp.com`) is verified in SendGrid. - You can customize the email body / template as needed. --- ## 6. Deploy the Function ```bash npm run deploy ``` The CLI will upload the `sendWelcomeEmail` function to Firebase and expose it as a Cloud Function that listens to `auth.user()` events. --- ## 7. Verify It Works 1. Create a new user in your Auth test console or via your signup flow. 2. Check: - Firestore / Realtime DB > `users/` – you should see the new user doc. - SendGrid dashboard > Verified Recipients > Sent Emails – you should see the welcome e‑mail. - The console output of the function will say “Welcome email sent to …” --- ## 8. (Optional) Local Testing If you want to test locally: ```bash firebase emulators:start ``` It will spin up local emulators for Auth & Firestore. Trigger a local Auth event and watch the logs. --- ## 9. Security Tips - **Never commit `.env` or `serviceAccountKey.json`.** - Use Replit Secrets manager: 1. Go to **Secrets** (the lock icon). 2. Add keys `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`. 3. Replit automatically injects them into `process.env`. - Keep your SendGrid key restricted to the “mail.send” permission only. --- ## 10. Next Steps - **Add unsubscribe feature** in the email if you send newsletters. - **Template system**: use Handlebars or MJML for richer emails. - **Analytics**: Integrate a webhook to log delivery events. That’s it! Now every time a user signs up, a personalized welcome email will be sent out automatically. Happy coding!
